intro_html: Sweet, savory teriyaki beef over rice, prepped ahead so weeknights run themselves. You get 44 grams of protein per bowl for about $5.98 (at everyday cost), and the pan makes 14 servings. All the flavor of the food-court plate, none of the food-court price.
cost_closing_html: About $5.98 a bowl (at everyday cost) for a high-protein dinner that beats takeout on price and macros.
portion_html: Each of the 14 bowls carries 44 grams of protein at just 593 calories, keeping this one light, sweet, and filling.
upsell_html: Food-court flavor, home-cook price, and a fridge full of dinners already handled. Members get every recipe in the Meal Prep section, plus the full library of money lessons and tools, all for $1 a month.
shop_smart: Honey and hoisin do the heavy lifting here, so skip the bottled teriyaki sauce that charges extra for the same sweet-savory mix.
A bag of frozen broccoli is the cheapest veg in the recipe and keeps for weeks, so lean on it.
One red bell pepper adds color and crunch, but green peppers are cheaper if you want to shave a little more off the total.
make_it: Brown 4.9 pounds of 93/7 ground beef with the chopped onion, then drain.
Steam the broccoli florets and sliced red bell pepper until crisp-tender.
Whisk the soy sauce, hoisin, honey, beef broth, sesame oil, garlic, ginger, and cornstarch into a glaze.
Pour the glaze over the beef and simmer until it thickens and coats the meat.
Serve the teriyaki beef and veggies over rice in each container.
